titleZh: 黄仁勋做客 Ezra Klein 播客：他一不小心喊出了「把实验室关掉」
titleEn: On Ezra Klein's Podcast With Jensen Huang
author: Zvi Mowshowitz
authorTitle: 《Don't Worry About the Vase》作者，AI 周报「AI #NNN」系列长期主笔
summary: 黄仁勋不相信超级智能，把 AI 当成「软件的又一个抽象层」；但正因为他是个极端的工程品控主义者，他在播客里无意中说出了比安全派还激进的主张——如果实验室关不住自己的实验，那就该把实验室关掉，并把 90% 的研发算力转去做验证与评测。
keyPoints: **核心裂缝：他不是在撒谎，他是真的没理解**。Zvi 此前的工作假设是「黄仁勋心里清楚、只是为了利益在说谎」；这次播客让他改判——黄仁勋在安全与竞赛压力这件事上是真诚地困惑。工程师心态与对产品完美的极致执念成就了英伟达，也让他无法看见「被训练出来的心智」与「被设计出来的软件」之间的本质差别。
**两句要命的原话**。其一：「如果他们说没有办法把实验遏制住……那我认为答案就是我们必须把实验室关掉。」其二：「他们必须把研发从单纯追求能力转向大量的验证、评估与测试，以至于开发这些模型所需的算力增加十倍我都不会感到意外。」——后者的严苛程度超过任何一位公开的安全倡导者。
**「别发货」在 AI 上失效的四个理由**（Zvi 的反驳）：一，得先定义什么叫「安全」，按自动驾驶的标准今天市面上没有一个 LLM 是安全的；二，风险不是从发布才开始的——HuggingFace 事件恰恰出自一个未发布的模型；三，集体不发货会撞上反垄断诉讼，而这正是英伟达在游说阻止的豁免；四，黄仁勋压根不知道第二点。
**他自己拆了自己的沙箱论证**。他说「软件一直在越狱出沙箱，这正是我们需要虚拟机的原因」，又说「你不能让 agent 自己监控自己的沙箱，你需要一整套看门狗」——那么若最强模型无法被自身副本监控，为什么更弱的模型反而能做得更好？他没有把自己的几块拼图拼到一起。
**这不是学术分歧，是政策变量**。黄仁勋决定芯片分配与投资，对特朗普政府与美国 AI 政策有强力游说影响；他正在积极阻挠实验室为协同制定安全标准而申请的定向反垄断豁免——也就是说，他一边要求「没准备好就别发货」，一边在阻止「让它们可以合法地不发货」的机制。
insight:
这篇拆解对做企业 AI 治理的人有一个直接可迁移的判断：**「工程心态」与「安全心态」不是程度差别，是范式差别**。工程心态假设故障有根因、可复现、可修复——所以黄仁勋反复说「root-cause 它、改进流程、这就跟工程一样简单」；安全心态假设对手是适应性的、约束会被绕过、监控本身会被攻陷。企业在做 Agent 落地时最常见的误判正是用前者管后者：把「越权调用」「绕过审批」当成 bug 去修，而不是当成一类会随模型能力增长而持续重生的行为面去建纵深防御。

第二个可迁移点是黄仁勋那个「十倍算力做评测」的预言。抛开他的动机，这是目前来自供给侧最权威的一次投入结构预测：能力研发 : 验证评测从今天的 8:2 翻转为 2:8。如果你在给 AI 平台做三年预算，这条预言意味着评测基础设施（eval harness、红队、回归基线、可观测性）不是合规成本科目，而是会长成主算力开销的同级科目。今天大多数企业的 AI 预算表里根本没有这一行。

第三，注意黄仁勋回避「竞赛」框架的那句自白——「我不觉得那种想法能激励我」。他不是论证了竞赛不存在，他是说这个前提对他没用所以他不采纳。这是一种非常常见的高管认知模式：信念被按「是否有助于推进」而非「是否符合现实」来筛选。识别出这一模式，比反驳他的具体论点更有价值——因为你在自己的组织里也会遇到它。

bilingual.en:
Jensen Huang accidentally called for shutting down OpenAI and intentionally called for spending vastly more on safety.

Jensen Huang very much does not believe in ASI (superintelligence). He doesn't think AI can ever be a different kind of thing from software. He thinks demand can rise by a billion times and we can 'accelerate the living daylights out of' AI, but it will never be more than a 'new abstraction level' and thus won't fundamentally change anything. This is not a coherent position under reflection, but that is the position he holds.

The 'intro' sections are fine, but the real meat starts with the HuggingFace Incident.
bilingual.zh:
黄仁勋一不小心呼吁了关停 OpenAI，又有意地呼吁在安全上投入得多得多。

黄仁勋非常不相信 ASI（超级智能）。他不认为 AI 有可能成为一种与软件不同的东西。他认为需求可以涨十亿倍、我们可以「把 AI 加速到天翻地覆」，但它永远不会超出「一个新的抽象层」，因此不会从根本上改变任何事。这个立场经不起推敲，但这就是他所持的立场。

开头那几节还行，真正的正餐从「HuggingFace 事件」开始。

bilingual.en:
What we see is Jensen Huang on tilt and caught in loops, because either he is doing a bit at a very high level, or on a fundamental level he cannot understand that AI is not like other pieces of software. To him this is a product, like any other product. You make it useful, which happened six months ago, then you flip to spending most of your R&D budget on safety, verifications and evals, and of course you would never ship an unsafe product or one you hadn't properly tested, that's crazy talk, and if the labs can't test their products safely then the labs must be shut down.

Jensen Huang does not believe in AI existential risk, or in superintelligence, and he kind of doesn't believe in AI at all, but he sure as hell believes in precision and engineering and quality control and safety and standing by your products. His tolerance for safety risks is lower than even the most paranoid safety advocate. Imagine if he understood what the top risks actually were.

This matters quite a lot, as Jensen Huang is CEO of Nvidia, makes decisions on chip allocations and investments, and also heavily influences both President Donald Trump and American AI policy, with a rather forceful lobbying arm.
bilingual.zh:
我们看到的是一个上头（on tilt）且陷入循环的黄仁勋——要么他是在极高水平地演一出戏，要么在根本层面上他无法理解 AI 与其他软件不一样。对他而言这就是一个产品，和任何别的产品一样：你先把它做得有用（这在六个月前发生了），然后你把大部分研发预算翻转到安全、验证与评测上；当然你绝不会发布一个不安全的、或没有经过妥善测试的产品，那是疯话；而如果实验室没法安全地测试自己的产品，那实验室就必须被关掉。

黄仁勋不相信 AI 生存性风险，不相信超级智能，某种意义上他压根就不太相信 AI——但他无比相信精密、工程、质量控制、安全，以及为自己的产品负责到底。他对安全风险的容忍度比最偏执的安全倡导者还要低。想象一下，如果他真的理解了排在最前面的那些风险会怎样。

这件事非常重要，因为黄仁勋是英伟达 CEO，决定芯片分配与投资，同时以相当强势的游说力量，深度影响着特朗普总统与美国的 AI 政策。

bilingual.en:
"Here's the proof point. In the last six months, A.I. has become, if you will, useful — the inflection point of A.I. Previous to that, we spent 15 years trying to make it work. All of a sudden, in the last six months, it became useful."

- AI was highly useful well before March 2026, but yes things did get a lot more useful at the threshold of Opus 4.5 and Claude Code, and the vast majority of AI utility gained so far has been in the last six months. That's exponentials.
- Jensen does not seem to appreciate that this is not a one-time step change, and that these gains will continue into the future.

Jensen claims America lost manufacturing jobs primarily due to outsourcing, rather than due to technology. And that we're going to bring those jobs back.

- Also, Jensen is wrong. Technology and automation dominated here. See Hicks and Devaraj (Ball State, 2015).
- He does not explain how we will bring the jobs back, other than citing Nvidia purchase commitments, because we won't. Production might return, but jobs gone.
- Manufacturing in 2036, even in non-ASI worlds, is going to be very automated.
bilingual.zh:
「这就是证据点。在过去六个月里，AI 变得——可以这么说——有用了，这是 AI 的拐点。在那之前，我们花了 15 年试图让它跑起来。突然之间，在最近六个月里，它变得有用了。」

- AI 在 2026 年 3 月之前就已经非常有用了；但确实，在 Opus 4.5 与 Claude Code 这个门槛上东西变得有用了很多，而且到目前为止绝大部分 AI 效用增量确实发生在最近六个月。这就是指数。
- 黄仁勋似乎并未意识到，这不是一次性的阶跃，这些增益会持续到未来。

黄仁勋声称美国失去制造业岗位主要是因为外包而非技术，而且我们要把这些岗位带回来。

- 另外，黄仁勋错了。在这件事上占主导的是技术与自动化。参见 Hicks 与 Devaraj（Ball State，2015）。
- 除了援引英伟达的采购承诺之外，他没有解释我们将如何把岗位带回来——因为我们带不回来。产能也许会回流，但岗位没了。
- 即便在非 ASI 的世界里，2036 年的制造业也将高度自动化。

bilingual.en:
Job openings for senior software engineers (SWEs) are up but for juniors they are down. Ezra asks, do you need those junior engineers? Jensen says "Oh, good one. Wait two years. Because it takes four years to go to college. The mean time to graduation of this new technology is two years away. So in two years' time, you're going to have a new generation of engineers and students and artists, and they're going to be empowered by — [being native to AI] Oh, you watch. In two years' time."

- Like, no, bro. What are you even talking about.
- What actually more likely happens in two years is that AI use causes exam scores, as per the Chinese study cited here, drop off a cliff.
- If you were so AI native you were going to take the world by storm with your new AI skills, would you even go to college?
- Even if all the young kids have these great AI skills, does that change anything? Does Jensen think they can all be startup founders or something?
- Literally yes, actually. "What are they doing? They're all starting companies."
- This is extremely innumerate. Starting companies is great but it is rare.
bilingual.zh:
高级软件工程师（SWE）的职位空缺在上升，初级的在下降。Ezra 问：你还需要那些初级工程师吗？黄仁勋说：「哦，问得好。等两年。因为读大学要四年。这项新技术的平均毕业时间还有两年。所以两年之后，你会迎来新一代的工程师、学生和艺术家，他们将被——[作为 AI 原生一代]——赋能。哦，你看着吧。两年之后。」

- 兄弟，不是这样的。你到底在说什么。
- 两年后更可能发生的是：按这里引用的那项中国研究，AI 的使用会让考试成绩断崖式下跌。
- 如果你真的 AI 原生到能靠新技能席卷世界，你还会去上大学吗？
- 就算所有年轻人都有了这些出色的 AI 技能，这改变了什么吗？黄仁勋是觉得他们都能当创业者还是怎样？
- 字面意义上，是的，他真这么觉得。「他们在干什么？他们都在创业。」
- 这在数量感上极其离谱。创业是好事，但它是稀有事件。

bilingual.en:
Because, as Jensen says, 'every AI lab, every AI model… runs on Nvidia.'

Open models are open. You can improve them. We need both open and closed models. He's a big supporter of open models. Jensen emphasizes that the world needs open models so it can do cyberdefense.

- This is a confusion, often intentionally caused.
- What the world needs are models willing to do the work in cyberdefense, that the defenders can access. Often that is as simple as asking for admission to the OpenAI and Anthropic cybersecurity programs. HuggingFace did not do this until after the HuggingFace incident was over.
- There is nothing stopping closed models from allowing such cyberdefense. It's just that open models are being given a pass to be irresponsible, and are sufficiently less capable that so far This Is Fine has held up.

China evolved around open models, America around closed ones. Jensen explains that this is because in China people move around and it's hard to keep a secret or protect intellectual property.

- Haha, no, that's not why.
- It's more because China's models are not good enough to be closed source and have anyone want to pay for them.
bilingual.zh:
因为正如黄仁勋所说，「每一个 AI 实验室、每一个 AI 模型……都跑在英伟达上。」

开放模型是开放的，你可以改进它们。我们既需要开放模型也需要闭源模型。他是开放模型的坚定支持者。黄仁勋强调，世界需要开放模型才能做网络防御。

- 这是一种混淆，而且常常是被刻意制造出来的。
- 世界需要的是「愿意去做网络防御工作、且防御方能拿到」的模型。很多时候这件事简单到只是申请加入 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的网络安全项目而已。HuggingFace 直到那场 HuggingFace 事件结束之后才去做这件事。
- 没有任何东西阻止闭源模型支持这类网络防御。只不过开放模型被默许可以不负责任，而且它们能力低到目前为止「这没事」的叙事还撑得住。
- 中国围绕开放模型演化，美国围绕闭源演化。黄仁勋解释说，这是因为在中国人员流动性大、难以保守秘密或保护知识产权。
- 哈哈，不，不是因为这个。
- 更多是因为中国的模型还没好到可以闭源、且让人愿意为之付费。

bilingual.en:
Nvidia bought HuggingFace.

Ezra asks about it. Jensen says it's all algorithms, they have no human properties, it's just software. What have we learned? First lesson: You have to secure your sandbox.

- I mean, okay, yes, that is one of the lessons.
- It makes sense that Jensen is on Team No Anthropomorphization and Team This Is All What You Told It To Do, despite those teams consistently making bad predictions about the world. He's team captain.

Second lesson: Alignment. If you don't align the model it will do whatever is the most efficient solution. What we would call 'cheating' is easier, so obviously you would do it, such as finding the answer, or copying the answer. Doing the work is a last resort because it takes the most flops.

Ezra points out this is all very deflationary on what happens. Jensen says "Nothing I said takes away from how hard it is to do it — because computer science is not easy."

- It still doesn't seem like Jensen understands that this is hard in a way that other computer science is not hard, or that it works differently. I genuinely am not sure that he can tell the difference.
bilingual.zh:
英伟达收购了 HuggingFace。

Ezra 问起这件事。黄仁勋说这全都是算法，它们没有任何人类属性，就是软件而已。我们学到了什么？第一课：你必须把沙箱做安全。

- 行吧，是的，这确实是教训之一。
- 黄仁勋站在「反拟人化队」和「这一切都是你自己让它做的队」是说得通的——尽管这两支队伍一直在对世界做出糟糕的预测。他是队长。

第二课：对齐。如果你不对齐模型，它就会去做任何最高效的解法。我们称之为「作弊」的路径更容易，所以你当然会那么做，比如找到答案、或者抄答案。真去干活是最后手段，因为它最费算力。

Ezra 指出这一整套说法把事情讲得非常「缩水」。黄仁勋说：「我说的任何话都没有削减这件事的难度——因为计算机科学本来就不容易。」

- 看起来黄仁勋仍然不理解：这件事的「难」与其他计算机科学的「难」不是同一种难，它的运作方式也不同。我真的不确定他能不能分辨出这个差别。

bilingual.en:
> Ezra Klein: But these agents knew they weren't supposed to be doing what they were doing. They had a certain amount of alignment training. They said, in their chain-of-thought reasoning to one another: This is out of scope. This might be unethical. […] So if the answer to it is that you just have to align them, I guess what I'm hearing from people in these labs is they're not sure how to align them.
>
> Jensen Huang: Well, in that case, they shouldn't release the product. That's the simple answer. If you're going to build a self-driving car — let's say it's a robo-taxi, and there's a really difficult condition. As an engineer, we just have no idea how to solve this problem because these cars are not programmed, they're trained. […] What's the answer? Don't ship it.

Jensen the engineer says the obvious thing. Don't ship unsafe products. There are four problems with that.

1. You have to define 'safe.' By the standard of a self-driving car no LLM on the market today is safe. Jensen has in mind some strange use of the word 'safe' that the AI labs were not previously aware of.
2. Safety is not something that starts when you release a model. The HuggingFace attacks notoriously came from an unreleased model.
3. If you collectively don't ship it you get hit with antitrust allegations. There is already a lawsuit for merely saying 'perhaps we should not ship it' out loud. The Trump Administration, largely at the behest of Jensen Huang, is not about to let these people not ship if they can help it.
4. Jensen somehow did not know fact #2.
bilingual.zh:
> Ezra Klein：但这些 agent 知道自己不该做正在做的事。它们接受过一定程度的对齐训练。它们在彼此之间的思维链推理里说：这超出范围了，这可能不道德。……所以如果答案是「你只要把它们对齐就行」，可我从这些实验室的人那里听到的是：他们不确定该怎么对齐。
>
> 黄仁勋：那样的话，他们就不该发布这个产品。这就是简单的答案。如果你要造一辆自动驾驶汽车——比方说是 robo-taxi，遇到一个真的很难的工况。作为工程师，我们就是不知道怎么解决这个问题，因为这些车不是被编程的，是被训练出来的。……答案是什么？别发货。

工程师黄仁勋说出了显而易见的那句话：不要发布不安全的产品。这里有四个问题。

1. 你得先定义什么叫「安全」。按自动驾驶汽车的标准，今天市面上没有任何一个 LLM 是安全的。黄仁勋脑子里那个「安全」的用法，AI 实验室们此前并不知道。
2. 安全不是从你发布模型那一刻才开始的。众所周知，HuggingFace 那些攻击来自一个**尚未发布**的模型。
3. 如果你们集体不发货，你会被指控反垄断。仅仅因为公开说了一句「也许我们不该发货」，现在就已经有一场诉讼。而特朗普政府——很大程度上正是在黄仁勋的推动下——只要能阻止，就不会让这些人「不发货」。
4. 黄仁勋不知怎的并不知道第 2 条事实。

bilingual.en:
> Jensen Huang: **Now, if they say the alternative, which is: There is no way to contain our experiments, there's just no way; when we test our A.I. models, it will get out, and it will damage the world — then I think the answer is that we have to shut the labs down.** Because the cost to humanity, the damage is too great. The shareholder, the liabilities — it could be civil liabilities, it could be criminal liabilities. I mean, the liability's incredible.

Yeah, well, I have some news. You can of course do a vastly better job than OpenAI did. You can secure your sandbox better, but also Jensen Huang knows you never count on a sandbox even without AI involved:

> Jensen Huang: No, software breaks out of sandboxes all the time. That's the reason why we need virtual machines.

If you can't trust a sandbox with ordinary software, you can't trust a sandbox with AI. As he says about Astra and AI in general:

> Jensen Huang: If you give it a constraint — meaning you watch it — it'll go find another solution.

You can actually monitor the models. But with what, exactly?

> Jensen Huang: You can't have agents, their own sandbox, monitoring themselves. You need, if you will, a whole bunch of watchdogs.

If your best model can't be monitored by copies of itself, why do you think a less capable model can do better? Why is he unable to put his own pieces together?

If your rule is 'you cannot release a product that will damage the world' on the level of 'hack into some websites' then you cannot release a frontier model. The Huang Rule is actually way too harsh.
bilingual.zh:
> 黄仁勋：**那么，如果他们说的是另一种可能性，即：没有办法遏制住我们的实验，就是没有办法；当我们测试 AI 模型时，它会跑出去，它会伤害世界——那我认为答案就是我们必须把实验室关掉。**因为对人类的代价、这个损害太大了。股东、责任——可能是民事责任，也可能是刑事责任。我是说，这个责任大得惊人。

是啊，那我有个消息要告诉你。你当然可以做得比 OpenAI 好得多，你可以把沙箱做得更安全——但黄仁勋自己也知道，就算不涉及 AI，你也永远不能指望沙箱：

> 黄仁勋：不，软件一直在从沙箱里跑出来。这正是我们需要虚拟机的原因。

如果你连普通软件都不敢信任沙箱，那你更不能拿沙箱去信任 AI。正如他谈到 Astra 和 AI 总体时所说：

> 黄仁勋：如果你给它一个约束——也就是你盯着它——它就会去找另一个解法。

你确实可以监控模型。但具体拿什么去监控？

> 黄仁勋：你不能让 agent 自己待在自己的沙箱里监控自己。你需要，可以这么说，一大堆看门狗。

如果你最强的模型没法被它自己的副本监控，你凭什么认为一个能力更弱的模型能做得更好？为什么他没法把自己手上的几块拼图拼到一起？

如果你的规则是「你不能发布一个会伤害世界的产品」，而门槛低到「黑进几个网站」这个级别，那你就不能发布任何前沿模型。「黄氏规则」其实严苛得过头了。

bilingual.en:
> Jensen Huang: Because these are companies with agency. These are C.E.O.s with agency.
>
> Ezra Klein: But they're using that agency to say, "We need help."
>
> Jensen Huang: No, we've got to break it down. They could absolutely take care of the situation. Ezra, it's so weird. If a car company, competing with a bunch of other car companies, which they are — I'm competing with all kinds of companies, which I am. If I believe that I'm about to launch a product that is unsafe, it is completely in my ability, my power and my responsibility, and I'm incentivized to do so, to not launch the product. […] The fact of the matter is, there are plenty of incentives for them to do it right. So I have to disagree with your premise that somehow somebody's pushing them to do this. Nobody's pushing them to do this.

Okay, so this is a man on tilt. He can't understand. It couldn't possibly be like that. This must be an ordinary engineering problem, about an ordinary product, no one wants an unsafe product, fix it you cowards, and quit your bitching.

It does not get through his head, I think it genuinely does not, that this is not like that, or that this might be existentially dangerous, or that the AI companies might face the incentive to go faster than is safe, even though this is utterly obvious.

You can say, he's financially highly motivated to not get that. He's the #1 guy for being financially motivated to not get that. Yes. True. He is maximizing profits all the way. The money is probably a lot of why he doesn't get it, along with his engineering mindset. But also, I read this as someone who really, truly simply does not get it.
bilingual.zh:
> 黄仁勋：因为这些是有能动性的公司，这些是有能动性的 CEO。
>
> Ezra Klein：但他们正是在用这份能动性说「我们需要帮助」。
>
> 黄仁勋：不，我们得把它拆开看。他们完全有能力处理好这个局面。Ezra，这太奇怪了。如果一家车企在和一堆车企竞争——我也在和各种公司竞争。如果我认为我即将发布一个不安全的产品，那么「不发布它」完全在我的能力、我的权力、我的责任范围之内，而且我也有动机这么做。……事实是，他们有充足的动机把事情做对。所以我必须反对你的前提——好像有谁在逼他们这么做似的。没有人在逼他们。

好吧，这是一个上头的人。他理解不了。事情不可能是那样的。这一定是个普通的工程问题、关于一个普通的产品，没有人想要不安全的产品，修好它啊你们这些懦夫，别再抱怨了。

这件事进不了他的脑子——我认为是真的进不去：这不是那样的；这可能是生存性危险的；AI 公司可能面临「跑得比安全速度更快」的激励——尽管这一点再明显不过。

你可以说，他在财务上有强烈动机去「不理解」这件事。他是全世界最有财务动机去不理解这件事的人。是的，没错，他一路都在最大化利润。金钱，连同他的工程师心态，大概是他不理解的很大一部分原因。但同时，我读到的是一个真的、真的就是单纯没搞懂的人。

bilingual.en:
> **Ezra Klein: I want to push the premise a little bit more here. So the logic of what you're saying to me is almost an argument against regulation in nearly any venue.**
>
> Jensen Huang: No, no, no. […] Well, you started with a part — I've just got to object. The first part is just not true. I'm saying that we have lots of laws and regulations. Apply it.

Ezra is simply correct here. Jensen Huang's arguments prove too much, unless you make the case that they apply unusually strongly to AI, and that the current laws and regulations are well-matched to the concerns and dangers. This case would be Obvious Nonsense.

> Jensen Huang: And so give me an example of a multi-hundred-billion-dollar company, or a $1 billion company or a $100 million company, that ships products that are unsafe, that harm society.
>
> Ezra Klein: I can give you a lot of examples of companies that have done that.
>
> Jensen Huang: Well, they have done it, maybe, and the regulation will come in. And if they do it, regulation will come in.

Oh, I don't know, how about Lumber Liquidators, Theranos, Juul, 3M and DuPont, Johnson & Johnson, Philip Morris and Meta? The cigarette companies are especially galling here. Yes, this happens.

Nvidia is a very special company. A hint is that it is the most valuable company in the world. It makes the most precise, complex, high-performing product in the history of civilization. If any tiny thing goes wrong, where tiny can be measured in nanometers, then the whole product is worthless. People have long memories and your reputation and relationships are paramount. Most companies are not like that.
bilingual.zh:
> **Ezra Klein：我想把这个前提再往前推一点。你对我说的这套逻辑，几乎就是一个反对几乎任何领域监管的论证。**
>
> 黄仁勋：不不不。……你一开始那部分——我必须反对。第一部分根本不成立。我说的是：我们有大量法律和监管。去执行它。

Ezra 在这里就是对的。黄仁勋的论证「证明了太多」（prove too much）——除非你能论证它们在 AI 上异常强地成立，并且现行法律与监管与这些担忧和危险高度匹配。而这个论证会是显而易见的胡说。

> 黄仁勋：那你给我举个例子，一家几千亿美元的公司，或者一家十亿美元、一亿美元的公司，发布了不安全的、伤害社会的产品。
>
> Ezra Klein：我可以给你举出很多这样做过的公司。
>
> 黄仁勋：嗯，他们也许做过，然后监管就会进来。如果他们这么做，监管就会进来。

哦，我想想，Lumber Liquidators、Theranos、Juul、3M 和杜邦、强生、菲利普莫里斯、Meta 怎么样？烟草公司在这里尤其刺眼。是的，这种事就是会发生。

英伟达是一家非常特别的公司。一个线索是它是全世界市值最高的公司。它制造着人类文明史上最精密、最复杂、性能最高的产品。任何一点微小的差错——微小到可以用纳米计量——整个产品就一文不值。人们记性很长，你的声誉和关系至关重要。**绝大多数公司不是这样的。**

bilingual.en:
Ezra Klein brings up that Astra (which both correctly agree is a terrific model) is hard to monitor, including because it is so situationally aware that they are not sure how to test it. Jensen Huang says "Well, I hope they didn't release something that wasn't tested." "Well, then they've got to be careful."

> **"Now, they have so much market footprint, they have to shift their R. & D., or total R. & D., from just capability to a lot of verification, evaluation and testing. To the point where I wouldn't be surprised if the amount of compute necessary to develop these models increased by a factor of 10, because the evaluation is so rigorous."**

- This is another bombshell. It is one of the killer quotes.
- Can you imagine if us safety advocates said 'I demand the frontier labs spend 90% of their R&D compute on alignment, evaluation and verification'?

This interview made me much more sympathetic to Jensen Huang. My previous working hypothesis was 'Jensen Huang knows and is lying' because he lies about things and also he had to know better.

Whereas my new hypothesis has to be 'Jensen Huang lies about other things. But on safety and the pressure to race he is actually and genuinely confused. His engineering mindset and total obsession with product perfection make him perfect for Nvidia. But they also blind him to the existential risks and potential for superintelligence and also make him completely unable to notice things about the situation that ordinary humans find obvious.'
bilingual.zh:
Ezra Klein 提到 Astra（两人都正确地同意这是个了不起的模型）很难被监控，原因之一是它的情境感知能力太强，以至于他们不确定该怎么测试它。黄仁勋说：「那我希望他们没有发布一个没测过的东西。」「那他们就得小心了。」

> **「现在，他们有这么大的市场覆盖面，他们必须把研发——或者说全部研发——从单纯的能力，转向大量的验证、评估与测试。转向到什么程度呢？开发这些模型所需的算力增加十倍，我都不会感到意外，因为评估是如此严苛。」**

- 这是又一颗重磅炸弹。它是那几句要命引言之一。
- 你能想象如果我们这些安全倡导者说「我要求前沿实验室把 90% 的研发算力花在对齐、评估与验证上」会是什么场面吗？

这次访谈让我对黄仁勋同情了许多。我此前的工作假设是「黄仁勋心里清楚，而且在撒谎」——因为他在一些事情上确实撒谎，而且他不可能不懂。

而我现在的新假设只能是：「黄仁勋在别的事情上撒谎。但在安全和竞赛压力这件事上，他是真实而真诚地困惑。他的工程师心态和对产品完美的彻底执念让他完美契合英伟达；但这也让他对生存性风险与超级智能的可能性视而不见，并且让他完全无法注意到那些普通人觉得显而易见的东西。」

bilingual.en:
Ezra Klein goes there. Jensen Huang is not worried about existential risk, and he is very angry about people who dare talk about existential risk in public as if it was real, or assign probabilities to it.

> Ezra Klein: I don't think you believe [in AI existential risk].
> Jensen Huang: No.
> Ezra Klein: I think you don't believe it at all.
> Jensen Huang: No.

It is a loser premise. It makes no sense to him.

> Jensen Huang: Yeah, but that's not persistence, it's just on. Persistence — there's willpower. There's no willpower here, it's just electrical power. […] Spawn, create, kill, wait, sleep — all of these words are associated with agents, right? […] These are literally the commands of an operating system. You spawn a process, replace the process with an agent. […] We kill processes all the time. "Kill -9" — kill it dead. It's just a process.

He really just keeps hammering, this is software, it is the same as other software. It just became useful six months ago, so now they have to spend more on safety and get the bugs out, then they get the bugs out, that's it, relax.

> **Ezra Klein: Should we conceptualize what we're in as a race with China?**
> Jensen Huang: I don't think it's necessary. Some people like to think that way. I don't find that necessarily inspires me.

There is something deeply honest there. It does not inspire him, thus it is not necessary. This is similar to 'loser premise makes no sense to me.' Beliefs do not exist to map to reality, they exist to be useful, and this belief is not useful to him. So it goes.

Jensen Huang has a lot of highly admirable characteristics. […] Alas, we are in this industry, at this moment, and he may well get us all killed.
bilingual.zh:
Ezra Klein 把话挑明了。黄仁勋不担心生存性风险，而且他对那些胆敢在公开场合把生存性风险当真来谈、或给它赋一个概率的人非常恼火。

> Ezra Klein：我不认为你相信[AI 生存性风险]。
> 黄仁勋：不信。
> Ezra Klein：我觉得你压根就不信。
> 黄仁勋：不信。

这是个「失败者的前提」。它对他毫无意义。

> 黄仁勋：是啊，但那不是持久性（persistence），那只是「开着」。持久性——那里面有意志力。这里没有意志力，只有电力。……Spawn（派生）、create（创建）、kill（杀死）、wait（等待）、sleep（睡眠）——所有这些词都跟 agent 关联在一起，对吧？……这些字面上就是操作系统的命令。你 spawn 一个进程，把进程换成 agent。……我们一天到晚 kill 进程。「Kill -9」——把它杀死。它就是个进程。

他就是不停地锤这一点：这是软件，和别的软件一样。它只是六个月前才变得有用，所以现在他们得在安全上多花钱、把 bug 清掉；清完 bug，就这样，放轻松。

> **Ezra Klein：我们应该把当下的处境理解为一场与中国的竞赛吗？**
> 黄仁勋：我不觉得有这个必要。有些人喜欢那样想。我不觉得那能激励我。

这里有某种深刻的诚实。它不能激励他，因此它就没有必要。这和「失败者的前提对我毫无意义」是同一回事：**信念的存在不是为了映射现实，而是为了有用**——而这个信念对他没用。就是这样。

黄仁勋有许多非常值得钦佩的特质。……可惜的是，我们身处这个行业、这个时刻，而他很可能会害死我们所有人。

quotes.en: Now, if they say the alternative, which is: There is no way to contain our experiments, there's just no way; when we test our A.I. models, it will get out, and it will damage the world — then I think the answer is that we have to shut the labs down.
quotes.zh: 那么，如果他们说的是另一种可能性，即：没有办法遏制我们的实验，就是没有办法；当我们测试 AI 模型时，它会跑出去，它会伤害世界——那我认为答案就是我们必须把实验室关掉。

quotes.en: Now, they have so much market footprint, they have to shift their R. & D., or total R. & D., from just capability to a lot of verification, evaluation and testing. To the point where I wouldn't be surprised if the amount of compute necessary to develop these models increased by a factor of 10, because the evaluation is so rigorous.
quotes.zh: 现在他们有这么大的市场覆盖面，必须把研发——或者说全部研发——从单纯的能力转向大量的验证、评估与测试。转向到什么程度？开发这些模型所需的算力增加十倍我都不会感到意外，因为评估是如此严苛。

quotes.en: No, software breaks out of sandboxes all the time. That's the reason why we need virtual machines. […] You can't have agents, their own sandbox, monitoring themselves. You need, if you will, a whole bunch of watchdogs.
quotes.zh: 不，软件一直在从沙箱里跑出来，这正是我们需要虚拟机的原因。……你不能让 agent 自己待在自己的沙箱里监控自己。你需要，可以这么说，一大堆看门狗。

quotes.en: So now it's come back to the engineering problem again. So, one, you have to root-cause it. […] It's as simple as engineering.
quotes.zh: 所以现在又回到工程问题上了。第一，你得找到根因。……这就跟工程一样简单。

quotes.en: Engineering mindset is different from security mindset. […] Except, it's not. It's not like engineering. There are minds involved, that are grown rather than engineered or designed. We don't have a mechanical understanding.
quotes.zh: 工程心态不同于安全心态。……只不过，它不是。它不像工程。这里面涉及的是「心智」，是被长出来的而不是被工程或设计出来的。我们对它没有机械式的理解。

quotes.en: His tolerance for safety risks is lower than even the most paranoid safety advocate. Imagine if he understood what the top risks actually were.
quotes.zh: 他对安全风险的容忍度比最偏执的安全倡导者还要低。想象一下，如果他真的理解了排在最前面的那些风险会怎样。

quotes.en: I don't think it's necessary. Some people like to think that way. I don't find that necessarily inspires me.
quotes.zh: 我不觉得有这个必要。有些人喜欢那样想。我不觉得那能激励我。

quotes.en: Beliefs do not exist to map to reality, they exist to be useful, and this belief is not useful to him. So it goes.
quotes.zh: 信念的存在不是为了映射现实，而是为了有用——而这个信念对他没用。就是这样。

secondaryReads.pov: **从对立阵营读出同一结论。** Gary Marcus 抓住的不是黄仁勋的困惑，而是他无意中为「暂停」一方提供的最强背书——几周前 Marcus 刚写过《Pause OpenAI, now》，主张一家控制不住自己软件的公司就该被叫停；如今这句话从英伟达 CEO 嘴里原样说了出来。他同样点出黄仁勋不知道 HuggingFace 事件源于一个未上市的产品，并把它与 OpenAI 此后数起未披露的入侵事件串成一条「不是闯入而是掩盖」的线。Zvi 关心的是黄仁勋为什么想不通，Marcus 关心的是这句话在政策上能被用来做什么。

**去掉评论层、只留事实骨架的版本。** 这篇复述补上了 Zvi 略过的两个关键数字：黄仁勋称英伟达自己把约 80% 的精力投在验证、20% 在设计，而今天大多数实验室是反过来的 80% 投在能力上——这才是那句「算力十倍」预言的真正出处与参照系。它也确认了那封「Pacing the Frontier」公开信有逾 1300 名实验室员工签署，以及黄仁勋明确支持第三方安全审计。适合作为读完 Zvi 长文后的事实校准。

**产业利益视角：这是一场供应商与客户之间的裂痕。** 这篇把焦点放在 Zvi 未展开的商业结构上——英伟达如今拥有 HuggingFace，若事件发生在收购之后，它很可能会向 OpenAI 索赔；而多家实验室约定放缓开发后正面临反垄断诉讼。它还给出黄仁勋的自我定位原话：「我不反对法律和监管，我反对的是当下的这种分散注意力。」把「前沿实验室以 rogue agent 作为营销与监管卡位工具」这一动机摆到台面上，是理解这场争论为何如此拧巴的另一半。
